selection: Six primary 2026 publications; aggregate observations only; no personal records or full reports stored.

sources.title: 2026 Essential Facts About the U.S. Video Game Industry — official announcement and methodology

collection.year_note: Announcement labels this the 2026 survey; methodology states February 11–25 without repeating year.

sources.population: United States; participation estimates include ages 5–90. Adults report household members; players 8–17 answer with parental supervision.
sources.method: 20-minute online YouGov proprietary-panel survey; weighted on demographic/geographic variables and gamer participation.

observations.meaning: Play on a mobile device; multi-platform measure, not Android-only.
Puzzle is the leading reported mobile genre.

observations.base: Gen Z among total players 18+; subgroup n not given on HTML page
observations.meaning: Report playing to pass time or relax.

observations.base: Gen Z among total players 18+; subgroup n not given on HTML page

sources.locator: Announcement: Mobile leads the way and methodology. Data page: Motivations for playing video games, explicitly among total players 18+.
limitations: Overall Gen Z participation includes minors; motivation data separately state players 18+.
No puzzle-specific adult Gen Z subgroup, task error or retention estimate.
sources.access: Primary page read directly through web research tool.
sources.licence: Copyright ESA; no open redistribution licence established. Minimal paraphrased aggregates and one quote shorter than 25 words retained; full report not stored.

sources.title: Play on Purpose: The Motivations of Adult Gamers Age 50-Plus

collection.discrepancy: Research summary includes a May wave absent from press-release methodology; do not silently merge.

sources.population: United States, age 50+; game-player findings are not all adults.
sources.method: Probability-based NORC panel; approximately 90% online/10% phone; weighted to CPS and membership benchmarks. Qualitative interviews AI-moderated.
sources.locator: Research summary: numerical bullet list and methodology; press release: From the report and methodology.
sources.short_quote: Older gamers are not one audience
limitations: Typical sessions are not first sessions or puzzle-specific targets.
No experience or motor-skill coefficient follows from age.
sources.access: Official indexed excerpts read through web search; direct origin read returned HTTP 403. Full report/questionnaire not obtained.
sources.licence: Copyright AARP; no open redistribution licence established. Minimal paraphrased aggregates and one quote shorter than 25 words retained; full report not stored.

sources.organisation: Deloitte Center for Technology, Media & Telecommunications
sources.title: 2026 Digital Media Trends: Capturing always-on fandom between releases and seasons
sources.population: US consumers; fan subgroup; not exclusively mobile players.
sources.method: Online independent-firm survey, census-weighted. Gen Z defined as birth years 1997–2011.

observations.meaning: Social media is primary discovery route for TV, movies, music, games or events.
More likely to engage with entertainment recommended by fan community.

limitations: Gen Z includes minors; no adult-only estimate extracted.
Cross-media discovery cannot calibrate puzzle help, skill, spend or retention.
sources.access: Primary article and methodology read directly through web research tool.
sources.licence: Copyright Deloitte; no open redistribution licence established. Minimal paraphrased aggregates and one quote shorter than 25 words retained; full report not stored.

sources.title: Adults’ Media Use and Attitudes Report 2026
sources.population: UK adults aged 16+; individual statistics use their stated internet-user sub-bases.
sources.method: Mixed online-panel and face-to-face survey. Consolidated questionnaire differs from 2021–2024; trend comparisons indicative.

observations.meaning: Report spending too long on screens most days.
Rely solely on a smartphone for internet access.
Breadth of use and task-specific confidence predict performance better than age alone.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 6–7: key findings; p. 7: methodology (PDF indices 5–6).
sources.short_quote: confidence does not always align with ability
limitations: Includes ages 16–17; not adult-only Gen Z.
Media-literacy tasks are not game ability or accessibility diagnoses.
sources.access: Official PDF text read through web research tool; PDF not copied into repository.
sources.licence: Ofcom copyright/re-use conditions not independently established here. Minimal paraphrased aggregates and one quote shorter than 25 words retained; full report not stored.

sources.title: Adults’ Media Lives — Wave 21: 2026
sources.population: Purposively selected longitudinal UK panel; illustrative, not population-representative.
sources.method: 17 in-home interviews and three online; over half the panel followed for more than 15 years.

observations.meaning: Gaming provides social connection for some participants; life schedules can limit opportunities.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 3–4: methodology/limits; pp. 52–53: gaming context.
limitations: No prevalence, demographic weight or error-rate inference from 20 interviews.
No participant identities, biographies or quotations retained beyond methodological phrase.
